eventMetadata.context_description: The fragmented 2028 Democratic field, with no candidate consolidating broad support from donors, party factions, or early polling two years before the first contests, keeps trader consensus tightly clustered among Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff. The DNC's recent selection of South Carolina to open the primary calendar elevates diverse-state dynamics and could favor candidates with stronger appeal among key voting blocs. Name recognition sustains Harris while progressive energy and visibility boost AOC and Ossoff, whose 2026 Senate race performance remains a key variable. Executive experience and debate strength position governors like Newsom, yet the absence of a dominant figure leaves room for shifts from upcoming polls, endorsements, or legislative actions before Iowa or South Carolina voting.
